subject.title: fix(gateway): preserve pending replies on forced restart

question: Should forced gateway restart keep meaning immediate/no active-work wait, or may it use a bounded 5s best-effort drain to preserve pending replies?
rationale: The patch fixes a message-loss path by changing an operator-visible force-restart contract that current help and docs still describe as immediate.

options.title: Accept bounded force drain after proof
options.body: Require live forced-restart pending-reply proof and wording updates, then treat 5s best-effort drain as the new `--force` contract.

options.title: Keep force immediate
options.body: Pause or close this PR and pursue a different pending-reply recovery design that preserves the existing immediate force behavior.

options.title: Add an explicit mode
options.body: Ask for a separate opt-in flag or config shape if maintainers want both immediate force and bounded reply-preserving force semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded force drain after proof
recommendation.body: Require live forced-restart pending-reply proof and wording updates, then treat 5s best-effort drain as the new `--force` contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about user-visible gateway restart semantics, and this handle is connected to adjacent restart-shutdown recovery history and recent gateway lifecycle changes.
